name: Brutalism

influenced_by: Le Corbusier's béton brut (raw concrete) buildings
postwar Britain's need for fast, cheap public housing

garments: not a fashion look — an architectural movement

media.title: Alison and Peter Smithson's writing and buildings (coined "New Brutalism," 1953)

reacts_against: decorative postwar optimism and the expense of traditional materials, exposing raw concrete and structure honestly instead of disguising it.
revivals: a 2010s-20s design and photography revival ("brutalist web design," Instagram accounts dedicated to the buildings) largely reframing it as aesthetic rather than functional

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Exposed materials, unfinished concrete, minimalist compositions, geometry

findings: mostly muted — about 78% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
